articles.headline: Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz-inspired Liverpool beat poor Crystal Palace 3-1
articles.description: Florian Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal of the season as Liverpool beat struggling Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park.
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal of the season as Liverpool beat struggling Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park.

Under-pressure Eagles boss Pierre Sage's side showed promise in the first half, when they had a goal chalked off for offside, hit the crossbar, and forced Alisson Becker into several good saves.

But it was the familiar manner in which they conceded the 40th-minute opener to Alexis Mac Allister -- from a set-piece -- and after a promising spell, that would have especially frustrated Sage.

Wirtz, whose last Premier League goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds' advantage nine minutes into the second half.

Alexander Isak added to the visitors' lead in the 89th minute, but Andoni Iraola's side were denied a clean sheet after Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty.

The visitors got to work quickly, calling Dean Henderson into a low save with a Mac Allister effort in the first minute. But Palace soon enjoyed a brief spell deep in the Liverpool half, where Tyrick Mitchell delivered a ball into the six-yard box but Jorgen Strand Larsen could not angle himself to truly pose a threat to Alisson.

Action returned to Palace's final third, where Mac Allister attempted to fire home from a free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai forced a diving stop from Henderson, though the ball looked to be travelling wide.

Yéremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring in the 18th minute. The crowd rose in anticipation after the Spain international collected Mitchell's cross, then curled an effort -- which looked to have Alisson beaten -- off the crossbar. Pino had little time to rue the fine margins, as he was then called back into action from a corner, rising highest to meet it but directing it at the Brazil keeper for a straightforward save.

Strand Larsen, who had just been denied a shot after some good work by Virgil van Dijk and Milos Kerkez to close in, had the ball in the back of Alisson's net in the 33rd minute. The Norwegian's celebrations were cut short by the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check, but Palace kept the pressure on and there was a sharp effort from Daichi Kamada, which required another quick reaction from the Liverpool keeper.

Mac Allister, unmarked, then broke the deadlock, nodding home a Szoboszlai free-kick, no doubt too easily for Sage's liking, and Alisson preserved the lead when he saved from Quinten Timber and Adam Wharton. Wirtz made it two in the ninth minute of the second half, directing a low Bradley Barcola cross that had evaded every Eagle in the penalty area into the bottom-left corner.

Palace had a huge chance with just under 15 minutes remaining when Timber's replacement, Darío Osorio, squared to Pino. He was one on one with Alisson, who perfectly timed his response, rushing forward to smother the finish, then denied Jefferson Lerma, and Nketiah lashed an effort over.

articles.headline: Ben Johnson's Stanky Legg dance is Chicago Bears' latest postgame tradition
articles.description: As the weeks progress for the Bears, players eagerly await Johnson's dance, knowing that it signifies another win.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Ben Johnson faced a split-second decision as he strode past a gathering of coaches and front office members to where his players waited in the locker room at Soldier Field.

The Bears had just dismantled the Philadelphia Eagles 27-7 on "Monday Night Football," with third-string quarterback Case Keenum playing in place of an injured Caleb Williams. The postgame atmosphere was palpable, and the 40-year-old head coach was about to ignite the celebration even further.

Johnson's typical game-day demeanor resembles that of a stoic actuary calculating risk on a clipboard. At this moment, though, there was no plan, just vibes. And Johnson had lost his composure in the best way possible when he wound up his right arm before crossing it over his chest while lunging forward to wobble his left knee back and forth.

Johnson's version of the Stanky Legg hardly resembled the dance move popularized by the 2008 song by hip-hop group the GS Boyz, but his spur-of-the-moment celebration sent the locker room into a frenzy.

"Honestly, I had no idea," Johnson said. "Those guys were waiting for me like that, and so I didn't know what to do. That was a panic move is what it was."

The core of the dance move, which Johnson said he remembered teammates doing in high school in the 2000s, is simple. While shifting one's weight to one leg with the other extended out, the goal is to roll the extended leg in a loose circular motion while leaning back like you just stepped in something unpleasant.

Johnson had a big smile stretched across his face as he leaned into his rendition. Players watching shared laughs and cheers as their head coach let his guard down and showed off his jovial side.

"I [mess] with it," right tackle Darnell Wright said. "It's cool. I think the first one wasn't as good, but I think he's getting better week to week. He's improving. ... He just got to keep at it."

During his first season in Chicago, Johnson brought the "Good, Better, Best" chant to the Bears' locker room that he and his A.C. Reynolds High School teammates used to yell after wins. The high-energy cheer was instantly infectious and became a staple after wins that brought the locker room together.

Now, Johnson's Stanky Legg is part of the Bears' winning postgame traditions. Williams and several teammates joined their head coach after the Bears took down the Patriots on Oct. 22 by mimicking Johnson's version.

"It's something swaggy," cornerback Kyler Gordon said. "It's a new staple."

The following week, when Chicago beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle, Johnson added a stutter-step before he launched into his Stanky Legg. As the weeks progress for the Bears (6-2), players now eagerly await Johnson's choreography, knowing that it signifies another hard-fought win.

"It's becoming an iconic thing," wide receiver Rome Odunze said. "Obviously, the 'Good, Better, Best' [chant] is a classic. I love saying that, but seeing Ben doing his Stanky Legg after the game

articles.headline: Title challengers? Brighton see off Brentford to go above Man City, into second
articles.description: Diego Gómez scored another stunner as Brighton enjoyed a happy homecoming by climbing to second in the Premier League with a 2-0 win over 10-man Brentford at the Amex Stadium.
articles.body:
Diego Gómez scored another stunner as Brighton enjoyed a happy homecoming by climbing to second in the Premier League with a 2-0 win over 10-man Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

Albion have clocked up thousands of miles since thumping rivals Crystal Palace 5-0 three weeks ago, playing Conference League fixtures in Czechia and Spain either side of a trip to Liverpool and two visits to Manchester City.

Midfielder Gomez, who scored from the halfway line against Palace, rifled a thunderous, left-footed shot into the top left corner to give the high-flying Seagulls a 15th-minute lead.

Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off eight minutes later following a VAR review after catching Brighton midfielder Chema Andrés in the face with a raised arm.

Pascal Gross sealed a comfortable victory for the hosts with a 42nd-minute penalty awarded for Keane Lewis-Potter's shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic.

Albion's win was a seventh from 10 top-flight games this term and lifted them above City and back to within five points of leaders Arsenal, while eighth-placed Brentford remain on 14 points

Williams is taking the available options, which will need to continue versus a Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense that leans on zone pressures and three-deep coverage under Todd Bowles -- see it fast and get the ball out, as the Buccaneers own a top-five blitz rate.

In the run game, D'Andre Swift will continue to see heavy volume, but the Bears aren't the same team on the ground without Kyle Monangai, a pile pusher with high-end burst. And Bowles' unit is the league's best versus the run, allowing only 80 yards per game.

On the Buccaneers' side, we have to throw out the Week 8 tape versus the Falcons because of the weather in that one. However, Baker Mayfield, who didn't complete a pass in that matchup, has thrown for only 64 total yards in his first two games back from a thumb injury and will be tasked with managing the pocket versus a Bears front that now features defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. articles.headline: J.J. McCarthy wowing Giants after initial concerns over QB's 'maturity,' VP says
articles.description: Chris Mara said the Giants were concerned by J.J. McCarthy's maturity before the 2024 draft but says the QB has impressed his new team "on and off the field."
articles.body:
The New York Giants seriously considered drafting J.J. McCarthy out of college because they were wowed by his physical skills.

But McCarthy's development off the field over the past two-plus years also has impressed Giants brass, according to Chris Mara.

In a wide-ranging interview with the New York Post, Mara -- the brother of Giants owner John Mara and the team's senior vice president of player personnel -- discussed McCarthy's growth since being drafted by the Minnesota Vikings.

"We had him rated very high from a skill set. ... We weren't quite sure about the maturity level, but we loved his skill set," Mara told the Post, which published the interview Saturday. "He showed the ability to win, the ability to lead."

The Giants acquired McCarthy earlier this year in a trade with the Vikings, who used the 10th pick on the former Michigan star in 2024.

"Seeing him three years later, this is a completely different-looking person for me," Mara said.

The Giants debated using the No. 6 pick in 2024 on McCarthy before ultimately selecting wide receiver Malik Nabers. New York landed McCarthy less than three years later, sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings in the Sept. 28 trade.

After missing his entire rookie season because of a knee injury, McCarthy struggled with the Vikings last year, completing 57.6% of his passes with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He lost his starting job with the Vikings in training camp to Kyler Murray and was demoted to third string after an ankle injury kept him out of Minnesota's preseason finale.

But McCarthy has enjoyed success during his brief stint in New York, leading the Giants to an overtime upset victory against the Texans in Houston two weeks ago.

"I'm in awe when I watch him in practice," Mara said. "He's got a much better arm than I thought he ever had. He moves around great. Listen, the arrow's up on him too."

Mara reiterated that since joining the Giants, McCarthy has shown signs of maturity, which was an issue during his time with the Vikings.

"On the field and off the field [he looks different]," Mara said. "He's a terrific guy. He's matured. He's married now, has a kid."

McCarthy will make his second start for the Giants against the division rival Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich's Manuel Neuer set for spell on sidelines with foot injury
articles.description: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer sustained a partial ligament tear in his right foot and will be out of action for "the time being," the club said in a statement on Sunday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer sustained a partial ligament tear in his right foot and will be out of action for "the time being," the club said in a statement on Sunday.

Neuer had to go off with the injury shortly before halftime in Bayern's 2-1 Bundesliga win at Mainz on Saturday.

Bayern's statement did not give a specific length of layoff for the German goalkeeper, only stating it would be 'for the time being'.

"Manuel Neuer will be out of action for FC Bayern for the time being," the club said.

"The captain sustained a partial tendor tear in his right foot during the German record champions' 2-1 win against 1.FSV Mainz 05 on Saturday, as confirmed by an examination by the FC Bayern medical unit.

"Neuer was substitued shortly before half-time at Mainz."

Replacement goalkeeper Jonas Urbig filled in, as he has often done for the veteran Neuer this season. Urbig is viewed as Neuer's long-term successor at the club and the injury presents a chance to demonstrate he can eventually take the role.

The injury is another blow to Bayern's season following Vincent Kompany's battles with issues that saw him collapse at training. He was hospitalised and treated for meningeal irritation, which is an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

Neuer has only made five league appearances this season, while the 23-year-old Urbig has also made five, including his substitute appearance Saturday.

It was a bittersweet moment for Neuer as he also became Bayern's oldest Bundesliga player at 40 years and 225 days old in the game.

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 9
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's ranks are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Jaguars-Ravens game.

Teams on bye in Week 9: Steelers, Titans

Week 9 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ MIA

It's hard for a RB to average 28 fantasy points per game. Last season's leader averaged 24.5.
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs ARI

His updated receiving yards pace is 2,093. He is overcoming the team's QB.
 3. Puka Nacua, WR2 @ WSH

As long as he averages 12-plus targets per game, he will thrive.
 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 vs NYJ

Underwhelming games the past two weeks, but this week he faces the Jets.
 5. Brock Purdy, QB1 vs LV

Comes off the bye week ready to blast the Raiders' defense.
 6. Joe Burrow, QB2 @ ATL

 7. Drake Maye, QB3 vs GB

 8. CeeDee Lamb, WR3 @ IND

He's not the reason they lose games. Big game coming against the feeble Colts.
 9. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR4 @ MIA

He hasn't scored a TD since Week 3, but perhaps it changes versus the Dolphins this week.
 10. Josh Allen, QB4 @ MIN

The matchup with a stingy Vikings is reason for a lower ranking than typical. 
 11. Jared Goff, QB5 @ MIA

 12. Jayden Daniels, QB6 vs LAR

 13. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 vs LV

 14. Bijan Robinson, RB4 vs CIN

 15. Ja'Marr Chase, WR5 @ ATL

Incredible talent just had his first 100-yard receiving game in Week 8.
 16. Tee Higgins, WR6 @ ATL

The QB is so good that yes, the Bengals boast a pair of WR1 options. 
 17. Brock Bowers, TE1 @ SF

Yep, we basically view him as a top-five wide receiver now. He's that dominant.
 18. Dak Prescott, QB7 @ IND

His rushing TD versus the Cardinals saved what would have been a disappointing fantasy effort.
 19. Patrick Mahomes, QB8 vs NYJ

Bounced back from the Seahawks debacle with 25.44 fantasy points against the Broncos. 
 20. James Cook III, RB5 @ MIN

He has scored a TD in six consecutive games. The Vikings are tough, but you can't sit him.
 21. Jonathan Taylor, RB6 vs DAL

Will he still be a Colt on Sunday? Pay attention to the news. The Colts may sit him.
 22. Justin Jefferson, WR7 vs BUF

 23. Malik Nabers, WR8 @ PHI

 24. Chuba Hubbard, RB7 vs DEN

 25. Javonte Williams, RB8 @ IND

It feels like time for his second 100-yard rushing game of the season. 
 26. Kyren Williams, RB9 @ WSH

Only four running backs have more points, but he is sharing more touches now.
 27. Caleb Williams, QB9 vs TB

He averages 19.5 fantasy points. The Buccaneers are defending well, but you can't sit him
